entries.core_move: Map each time feature in $x(t)$ to t0/a in $x(at)$ for $a>1 and identify the resulting waveform as compressed toward t=0 with unchanged amplitudes$.
Map each time feature in $x(t)$ to t0/a in $x(at)$ for $0<a<1 and identify the resulting waveform as expanded away from t=0 with unchanged amplitudes$.

entries.lesson_title: How Time Scaling Moves Key Time Points
entries.core_move: Map each key time point t0 in $x(t)$ to t0/a in $x(at)$ by solving at=t0, then use that mapping to relocate starts, stops, corners, peaks, and zero crossings.
Convert a piecewise signal $x(t)$ into $x(at)$ for $a>0 by mapping each breakpoint t0 to t0/a and replacing t with at in the formula assigned to each scaled interval$.
Convert time-scaled exponentials by rewriting e^{$s(at)$} as $e^{(as)t}$ and interpreting a as changing the growth, decay, or oscillation rate in continuous time.

entries.lesson_title: Comparing Time Shifts and Time Scaling
entries.core_move: Distinguish time shifts from time scaling by mapping transformed arguments to key-time locations and deciding whether features translate by a constant offset or compress/expand relative to $t=0$.
